nz.name: Outdoor noise
nz.noproject: Open or start a project first.
nz.intro: Predict road, railway and industrial noise at points of this project by CNOSSOS-EU, the EU's common method. The ground comes from the project's existing-ground surface, barriers and buildings from its feature lines, roads and railways from its alignments.
nz.promise: A design aid; results are predictions, not measurements. Nothing in the project is changed and nothing is sent anywhere.
nz.source: Method: {method}. Read the texts on EUR-Lex.
nz.p.help: How often the weather bends sound down towards the ground on these paths, as a share of the period (0.82 = 82 %). The method takes this from your local weather; it gives no default, so set your own. Hours: the length of each period (12, 4 and 8 by default; the evening may be 2 or 3 hours with the day or night longer, Directive 2002/49/EC Annex I), used for Lden and for the working hours of point sources.
nz.ground.help: The ground types of the method's Table 2.5.a, with their G. Roads count as hard ground at the source and tracks on ballast as soft.
nz.lines.none: No alignments in this project. Draw a road or a track first.
nz.traffic.help: Vehicles per hour in each period and their average speed in km/h. Leave a row empty for none.
nz.rail.help: The trains of each period and the track, as the railway model reads them.
nz.err.json: That is not valid. Check the brackets and quotes.
nz.points.help: Industrial sources such as fans, pumps or plant: name, position (x, y in {u}), height above the ground (m), sound power per octave from 63 Hz to 8 kHz (eight numbers in dB) and the hours it runs in each period.
nz.name.label: Name
nz.barriers.help: Make any feature line a noise barrier (a thin wall that high above the ground), or a closed one a building (a block that high). Both block sound and reflect it.
nz.barriers.none: No feature lines in this project.
nz.recv.help: The points where the level is worked out, usually 4 m above the ground at a façade. Select survey points in the plan and add them, or type a position in {u}.
nz.recv.name: Receiver
nz.recv.nopick: Select one or more survey points in the plan first.
nz.limits.help: Your own targets in dB(A) for each period and for Lden. A receiver above one shows a warning in Problems. Leave empty for none.
nz.done: Receivers: {n}. Sources: {s}. Worked out in {ms} ms.
nz.issue.limit: {name}: {value} dB(A) in the {period} period, over your limit of {limit} dB(A).
nz.note.flat: This project has no existing-ground surface, so the ground is taken as flat.
nz.note.badline: The alignment {name} could not be read and was left out.
nz.note.badpoint: The point source {name} needs a position and eight sound power values; it was left out.
nz.note.emission: {name}, {period}: the emission could not be worked out ({why}).
nz.note.limits: Railway sound heights are taken above the track's design level where it has one, otherwise above the ground; the top of the rail is not drawn separately.
ac.out.note.nominal: Air absorption is worked out at the nominal octave frequencies.
ac.road.note.slow: A speed under 20 km/h is worked out at 20 km/h, as the method says.
ac.road.note.surfacerange: The speed is outside the range given for this road surface; its correction is used as given.
ac.road.note.cat5: Category 5 (open category) has no data in the method and is left out.
nz.alpha.help: Absorption αr is the share of sound the surface takes in when sound reflects off it (0 to 0.99), from the product's EN 1793-1 rating. Empty is 0: fully reflecting, the loudest case.
nz.refl.help: Sound reflected off barriers and building façades reaches the receivers as from a mirror source. The method asks for at least the first reflection; two take longer on big projects.
nz.note.reflections: Sound reflected off barriers and façades: {n} reflected paths (reflection order {order}).
nz.note.noreflections: Reflections are turned off, so barriers and buildings only block sound.
nz.note.lateral: Paths round the ends of barriers and the sides of buildings (point sources only, as the method says): {n}.
nz.note.trainbarrier: Sound bouncing between a train and a barrier close to the track is included ({n} paths).
nz.note.inside: Some sources or receivers are inside a building and were left out of those paths ({n}).
nz.note.raildir: Railways radiate more to the side than along the track; that direction is taken into account.
ac.pf.note.q1: Sound bouncing between a train and a barrier: the directive prints the reflection points as −(2i − q)·dB; they are taken as −(2i − 1)·dB, as its Figure 2.5.k shows.
ac.pf.note.eq248: Sound bouncing between a train and a barrier: the equivalent receiver height uses eq. 2.5.48 as printed (the sight line from the image source at height 0).
nz.note.graded: The ground between sources and receivers is the graded surface: the existing ground with the corridors, pads and grading cut and filled in.
nz.note.eg: The ground between sources and receivers is the existing ground (this project has no graded surface yet).
nz.note.design: Sources sit on the design profile of: {names}.
nz.note.badprofile: The design profile of {name} has errors, so its sources sit on the ground.
nz.design: Use design levels and the graded surface
nz.design.help: On: roads and tracks with a design profile sit on it, and sound travels over the graded surface (cuts, embankments and the road platform). Off: everything sits on the existing ground.
ac.ind.note.hours: Lden needs periods of 12, 4 and 8 hours, or an evening shortened to 2 or 3 hours with the day or the night longer, adding up to 24. Lden is not given.
ac.ind.note.shortevening: Lden is worked out with a {evening}-hour evening, as Directive 2002/49/EC Annex I allows.
ac.ind.note.silent: No source sounds in the {period} period; Lden counts it as silent.
ac.ind.note.notmapping: A receiver is {h} m above the ground. Strategic noise maps use 4 m (3.8 to 4.2 m) at the most exposed façade; other heights are fine for planning.
ac.ind.note.low: A receiver is {h} m above the ground; Directive 2002/49/EC Annex I never goes under {min} m.
nz.note.lden: Lden and Lnight as defined in Directive 2002/49/EC, Annex I: the incident sound, without the reflection from the receiver's own façade.
nz.issue.limit.den: {name}: Lden {value} dB(A), over your limit of {limit} dB(A).
